summary: Richard B. Russell Airport (RMG/KRMG) is a public general-aviation airport serving Rome, Georgia, located about five miles northwest of downtown. Named for U.S. Senator Richard B. Russell Jr., it has two runways and hosts the Wings Over North Georgia airshow. It primarily supports private, business, and flight-training aircraft, with no scheduled airline service.
faqs:
Q: Does Richard B. Russell Airport have commercial airline service?
A: No. RMG is a general-aviation airport with no scheduled passenger airline flights; it primarily handles private, business, and flight-training aircraft.

Q: What are the airport codes for Richard B. Russell Airport?
A: The IATA code is RMG, the ICAO code is KRMG, and the FAA identifier is RMG.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Rome, Georgia?
A: It is about 5 miles northwest of downtown Rome, typically a 10- to 15-minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Are rental cars or rideshare available at RMG?
A: Rental car availability is limited, so arrange one in advance; taxis and rideshare may serve the airport but can have longer waits, so confirm pickup before arrival.
transport_tips: The airport is a short drive north/northwest of downtown Rome and is easiest to reach by car. There is no regular public transit to the terminal, so plan on a taxi, rideshare, hotel shuttle, or rental car. On-site parking is available for general aviation visitors, but check with the FBO for after-hours access and gate codes.
local_tip: Frequent visitors call the FBO ahead for after-hours fuel and gate access, and they check the calendar for the Wings Over North Georgia airshow, which temporarily makes the airport very busy.
